To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the efficiency of the activation, execution and blackboard rating mechanisms of blackboard systems can be increased by a factor of approximately 7.6 and that the efficiency of execution can be increased by approximately four orders of magnitudes by using a condensed blackboard representation.
the time complexity for execution in a blackboard architecture can be improved significantly by the use of match networks, demons and a condensed representation.

(i) a knowledge source compiler for a class of blackboard systems can produce match networks for efficient knowledge source activation and demons for fast knowledge source execution; and (ii) a subclass of blackboards can be compiled down directly to the machine level for increased execution speed.

the development of efficient mechanisms for a class of blackboard systems and the demonstration of the effectiveness of these mechanisms in a general purpose blackboard shell.
